Class WorldMapElement

java.lang.Object
dev.tamboui.toolkit.element.StyledElement<WorldMapElement>
dev.tamboui.toolkit.elements.WorldMapElement
All Implemented Interfaces:
Styleable, Element
public final class WorldMapElement extends StyledElement<WorldMapElement>
Interactive offline world map element with keyboard and mouse pan and zoom.

The element owns a mutable MapState (the viewport); rendering is delegated to the stateless WorldMap widget, which letterboxes to a correct aspect ratio. Arrow keys (or h j k l) pan, +/- zoom, 0 resets to the whole world. The mouse wheel zooms toward the cursor and dragging with the left button pans. 

worldMap()
    .viewport(new MapViewport(-6, 16, 44, 58))
    .marker(new MapMarker(10.55, 55.37, Color.YELLOW))
    .title("Europe")
    .rounded();

    • preferredSize

      public Size preferredSize(int availableWidth, int availableHeight, RenderContext context)
      Description copied from interface: Element
      Returns the preferred size of this element.

      The availableWidth/Height parameters allow elements to adapt their dimensions based on constraints. Use -1 for unconstrained.

      Common patterns:

      • Text elements: height depends on width (text wrapping)
      • Aspect-ratio elements: both dimensions interrelated
      • Fixed elements: ignore available dimensions

      Return value semantics:

      • Positive values = known size (use as constraint)
      • Zero = explicitly zero-sized (element should collapse)
      • Negative (-1) = unknown size (element should fill available space)
      Parameters:
      availableWidth - the available width in cells, or -1 if unconstrained
      availableHeight - the available height in cells, or -1 if unconstrained
      context - the render context for CSS resolution, may be null
      Returns:
      the preferred size

    • handleKeyEvent

      public EventResult handleKeyEvent(KeyEvent event, boolean focused)
      Description copied from class: StyledElement
      Handles a key event by running the handler set with StyledElement.onKeyEvent(KeyEventHandler), if any.

      This is the single place an element's key handler runs: the event router does not call StyledElement.keyEventHandler() again for a StyledElement, to avoid running it twice for one key. A subclass that overrides this method must, for any key it does not consume itself, return super.handleKeyEvent(event, focused) rather than EventResult.UNHANDLED — otherwise a handler set with onKeyEvent is silently dropped, since the router will not run it.

      Specified by:
      handleKeyEvent in interface Element
      Overrides:
      handleKeyEvent in class StyledElement<WorldMapElement>
      Parameters:
      event - the key event
      focused - whether this element (or its subtree) has focus
      Returns:
      EventResult.HANDLED if the handler consumed the key, otherwise EventResult.UNHANDLED
